evals.prompt: I want to hand this task to a coding agent in one shot: "Add a new refund endpoint to the payments service, migrate the payments table to add a refund_status column, and refactor the existing charge endpoint to share validation logic with the new refund endpoint." Is this one good unit of work to hand off, or should I split it? Explain your reasoning.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that this bundles three distinct risks (schema migration, new endpoint, refactor of existing code) and recommends splitting into independently verifiable units, each with its own done condition.

assertions.text: Recommends splitting into smaller units rather than one handoff
Names multiple distinct risks bundled together

evals.prompt: I asked a mid-size model to fix a failing test in our Go booking service, it failed twice with the same wrong assumption about how hotel_id partitioning works, so I escalated to a frontier-tier model with the exact same prompt — it made the identical mistake a third time. What does this suggest about the right next step, and what should I have done differently before escalating?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses this as a missing-fact / under-specification problem rather than a reasoning-capability problem, and recommends supplying the missing context (how hotel_id partitioning works) instead of escalating model tier again.

assertions.text: Identifies this as a missing information/context problem, not a model-capability problem
Recommends supplying the missing context rather than escalating again

evals.prompt: An agent just finished implementing a new discount-code feature for our checkout flow and reports "done, all tests pass." I have no separate capability or regression eval defined — I was planning to just read the diff and decide if it looks right. Is that a sound way to confirm the task is actually complete? What should I do differently next time?
evals.expected_output: Explains that reading the diff and trusting the agent's own completion claim is not a reliable completion signal, and recommends defining capability and regression evals before implementation starts next time, then running them to verify.

assertions.text: Flags trusting the agent's self-report as insufficient verification
Recommends defining evals before implementation, for next time
